result.evidence:
Verified cda61e8 (branch v2/t-bank-area_and_volume) against base 9403838 (v2/t-bank). Each ran in its own detached worktree, both since removed, and nothing was committed. Scripts and dumps are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-workingmyassof-satbank/9030c288-6222-49fa-a25a-6e6802e22cd3/scratchpad/verify_aav/.

1. MCQ unchanged: PASS. For all 19 templates in TEMPLATES, I dumped every Item field except spr_mistakes for fmt default/mcq/spr and seeds 0-80, together with the 59 source items. The dump covers generate() and also 4 raw per-attempt template calls, including the exception each one raised, to catch any shift in rng draw order or exceptions. That is 23,144 lines, and cmp shows the base and branch files byte-identical.

2. Grid-ins unchanged except spr_mistakes: PASS. The same dump covers all 927 grid-ins. On base every spr_mistakes is [], and on the branch none is empty.

3. Are the spr_mistakes real: FAIL for measure.inverse. I checked 16 random grid-ins (seeded sample) by hand, plus one grid-in for each of 43 template variants and grid-in sources. forward, similar.linear, similar.area, scaling.percent, coord.circle_3pt, coord.triangle_area, coord.square_diagonals and circle.convert all check out: each value follows from the stem and its reason. None equals the key, none is None and none is repeated.
   In measure.inverse, every grid-in without then_measure (300 of 300 at seeds 0-299, 896 entries) also carries the forward-formula mistakes that the pool appends through _forward_mistakes(..., measure, dims). Their values are functions of the unknown answer, and their reasons describe computing the given measure from it. No student solving this stem would reach them. The MCQ path shows such a reason in only 34 of 300 items, and only as a fallback.
   Examples:
   - measure.inverse seed 31 (square, area 2,704, key s=52) names "found the perimeter instead of the area"=208, "doubled the side instead of squaring it"=104, "doubled the side, then squared it"=10,816 and "squared the perimeter"=43,264.
   - measure.inverse seed 7 (triangle, b=18, A=306, key h=34) names "added the base and height"=52 and "doubled instead of halving"=1,224.
   - Official sources: 2.6 and 2.11 name "added the base area and the height"=35 and 42. 3.12 (square prism, h=14, V=2,016, key s=12) names "did not square the base edge"=168 and "squared the height instead of the base edge"=2,352.
   A student who typed one of these values would have it filed under a reason that does not describe what they did.

4. Gate: PASS. `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m satbank check --topic area_and_volume` prints "Area and Volume [area_and_volume] PASS" (audit re-derived 5,700 items).

5. Coverage: PASS. tools/spr_coverage.py reports "area_and_volume 9 of 9". Every "spr" return in families/*.py passes spr_mistakes, including both returns in similar.linear. scaling.solid and coord.leg_from_area take fmt but have no grid-in branch, and the other 8 templates are MCQ-only.

The commit trailer is correct.

Separately, 468 of 1,800 grid-ins (seeds 0-199) carry an entry with π or a radical, such as "31π" or "4√97". Exact.gridin() raises ValueError on these, and scoring.grid_equal(typed, value.plain()) never matches them, so they can never name a typed answer.

defects.where: satbank/topics/area_and_volume/families/measure.py, inverse(), the spr return (~line 672) and the `for k, m in _forward_mistakes(shape.key, then_measure or measure, dims).items(): pool.setdefault(k, m)` loop above it
defects.what: spr_mistakes=gridin_mistakes(key, pick(pool, None)) takes the whole pool, including the forward-formula fallback entries. When then_measure is None, those describe computing the given measure from the unknown answer, not a wrong route to the answer. So every inverse grid-in names impossible mistakes: 896 entries across 300 items at seeds 0-299. Examples: seed 31, a square of area 2,704 with key 52, names 'found the perimeter instead of the area'=208 and 'doubled the side instead of squaring it'=104. Source 3.12 names 'did not square the base edge'=168. Sources 2.6 and 2.11 name 'added the base area and the height'=35 and 42. A student who types one of these values would be told a mistake they did not make.
defects.fix: Snapshot the inverse-specific pool before the _forward_mistakes loop, e.g. `own = dict(pool)`. When then_measure is None, pass `spr_mistakes=gridin_mistakes(key, pick(own, None))`. When then_measure is set, keep the full pool: there the forward mistakes are genuine, since the student found the edge and then misapplied the second formula. This draws nothing from rng and leaves the MCQ path untouched. Re-run the MCQ/SPR dump and the gate, and confirm no inverse grid-in ends up with an empty list.

defects.where: all 9 grid-in call sites (via satbank/item.py gridin_mistakes); mainly circle.convert ('gave the circumference instead', 'gave the area instead'), coord.square_diagonals ('gave the perimeter instead of the area' = 4√k), and measure.inverse π-valued entries
defects.what: Low severity. 468 of 1,800 grid-ins carry an entry whose value is irrational, such as 31π or 4√97. A grid-in can never match these: scoring.grid_equal('97.38', '31π') is False, and Exact.gridin() raises ValueError, so a to_question that formats value_text with .gridin() would crash. For rational keys the MCQ path never offers these values either, because assemble fills from same-form options first. The task's stated rules technically allow them, which is why this is low severity.
defects.fix: Filter out values that are not rational before building the list. One way is `if not m.value.is_rational: continue` in item.gridin_mistakes. The other is to filter at the call sites before passing, if the shared helper should stay as the base commit left it. Otherwise, tell the practice.to_question owner to format value_text with .plain() and never .gridin().
